title: The field that broke the consumers
outcome: A new required field, a compatibility check switched off to unblock a release, and every consumer that replayed history failed.

content.bookmark: Under BACKWARD compatibility, a new field needs a default so the new schema can still read old data. The compatibility check exists to refuse changes like this one.

check.prompt: In Avro, a reader's schema has a field the writer's data doesn't. What happens?
options: The reader's default is used; with no default, it is an error
check.why: Schema resolution fills a missing field from the reader's default. Without a default, reading fails.

check.prompt: What is Schema Registry's default compatibility mode?
check.why: BACKWARD: consumers using the new schema can read data written with the previous one.

check.prompt: Under BACKWARD compatibility, who upgrades first?
check.why: A BACKWARD-compatible schema can read old data, so consumers move to it first; producers follow.

check.prompt: In Protobuf, a field is removed. What should happen to its number?
options: Reuse it for the next new field
Mark it reserved and never reuse it
check.why: Protobuf identifies fields by number on the wire. Reusing a number makes old data decode into the wrong field.

caseStudy.setting: A travel company (fictional) publishes Booking events in Avro to bookings, with Schema Registry at its default BACKWARD compatibility. Several teams consume it; the analytics team regularly replays the whole topic to rebuild reports.

events.what: The bookings team adds a currency field with no default. The registry refuses the new schema as incompatible. Under release pressure, someone sets the subject's compatibility to NONE, and the schema is registered.
Consumers are upgraded to the new schema. Live data works. The analytics team's nightly replay from the start of the topic fails on the first old record.
Other teams that restart from older offsets fail the same way. Reports are a day late and the fix is disputed between teams.

pipeline: Bookings service · Avro serializer, schema version 7 adds currency (no default)
Schema Registry · subject bookings-value, compatibility switched from BACKWARD to NONE
bookings topic · 30 days of retention, old records written with version 6
Consumers · upgraded to version 7, some replay from the start
tasks: Why did reading old records fail?
What should the team have done when the registry refused the schema?

debrief.title: Why old records failed
text: Avro data carries no field names. The consumer reads each record with the writer's schema (version 6) and resolves it to its own (version 7).
Version 7 has currency; version 6 data doesn't. With no default to fill it in, resolution fails. Live records written with version 7 read fine, which is why the problem appeared only on replay.

debrief.title: What the refusal was telling them
text: BACKWARD compatibility means the new schema must read old data. The registry refused version 7 precisely because it couldn't. Switching to NONE removed the warning, not the problem.
The right change was to give currency a default (for example the company's base currency), which makes version 7 backward compatible.
BACKWARD is the default partly so consumers can rewind to the start of a topic, which is exactly what analytics does.

debrief.title: Guard rails
text: Only a schema owner can change a subject's compatibility, with review.
Check compatibility in the build, before deployment, so the failure is found by the team making the change.
Consider BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE, which checks against all earlier versions, not just the last.

takeaway: A new field needs a default to stay backward compatible.
The compatibility check refusing a schema is the system working.
content.honesty: If you haven't managed schema evolution, say so and explain the modes and the upgrade order. If you have a story of a breaking change, lead with it.

tasks: What would you put in the definition of done for a schema change?

debrief.title: Questions
text: "Who reads this event, and does anyone replay old data?"
"Why was the compatibility check turned off, and who decided?"

debrief.title: Definition of done
text: A schema change passes the registry's compatibility check without changing the mode.
Consuming teams are told before the change, with the upgrade order.

sayIt.question: How would you manage a change to an event that several teams consume?
points: Treat the event as an interface with a contract.
Know who consumes it and how: live or replay.
Require the change to pass compatibility checks, not bypass them.
Plan the upgrade order with consumers.
Make bypassing the check a reviewed decision with an owner.

tasks: How do you handle the release-pressure decision?
What do you tell the analytics team's users?

debrief.title: Release pressure
text: The shortcut saved a day and cost several teams more. Make the cost of bypassing a safety check visible when the decision is made.

debrief.title: Users
text: Tell report users which reports are late and when they'll be right.

sayIt.question: A team bypassed a safety check to hit a release date and broke other teams. How do you respond?
points: Fix the impact first and communicate it.
Review the decision blamelessly: what pressure, what information.
Make bypassing checks an explicit, owned decision.
Plan for interface changes in the roadmap, not under pressure.
Agree how teams change shared events.

tasks: How do you resolve this now?

debrief.title: Now
text: Register a version 8 that gives currency a default, restore BACKWARD, move consumers to version 8, rerun the replay.

debrief.title: Process
text: Schema changes reviewed by consuming teams; compatibility-mode changes need a named approver.

sayIt.question: How would you coordinate a schema change across teams?
points: Identify every consumer.
Agree the compatibility mode and upgrade order.
Check compatibility in the build.
Communicate dates and roll out consumers first under BACKWARD.
Keep compatibility-mode changes under approval.

tasks: What schema change would you make?
How do you check compatibility automatically?

debrief.title: The change
text: Version 8: currency with a default value. Set the subject back to BACKWARD (or BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE).

debrief.title: Automatic checks
text: Test each schema change against the registry's compatibility check in CI, before deployment.
Restrict who can change a subject's compatibility setting.

sayIt.question: Explain schema compatibility modes and how you evolve an Avro schema safely.
points: BACKWARD (default): new schema reads old data; consumers upgrade first.
FORWARD: old schema reads new data; producers first. FULL: both.
In Avro, add fields with defaults; a missing default breaks reading old data.
TRANSITIVE checks against all versions, not just the last.
In Protobuf, never reuse a field number; reserve removed ones.
